idiom_name: Roslyn CSharpSyntaxRewriter Visit methods plus SyntaxKind/SyntaxNode pattern matching
implementation_notes: Roslyn supplies both halves of the pattern: CSharpSyntaxRewriter descends an entire syntax node graph in depth-first order and lets each overridden VisitX method return a replacement node (or null to remove it), so the traversal belongs to the base class while the rule is the override plus a pattern match over SyntaxKind, node types and children. SyntaxNode.ReplaceNode and the With* methods perform surgical rewrites, DescendantNodes with is-patterns or a SyntaxWalker covers read-only matching, and SemanticModel is what a rule needs when the condition depends on types or symbols rather than shape. The classic structure therefore collapses into rewriter overrides; build a rule table over SyntaxKind only when the rules must be data shared across tools.
pitfalls: A rewriter that forgets to return the replacement (or to call base) silently does nothing, and a replacement built from scratch loses trivia - whitespace, comments and directives - so copy leading and trailing trivia explicitly.
Roslyn nodes are immutable: every edit builds new nodes through With* or ReplaceNode, and applying the wrong helper level produces a tree that no longer compiles or loses the original parent chain.
VisitIntoStructuredTrivia defaults to false, so rules that need to see directives or documentation comments match nothing until it is enabled - and enabling it changes the node stream the rules see.
